corrective v2 contract and distinct runner attempt record; prior v1 failed record retained separately

attempts.attempt_policy: One attempt under this corrective contract on its distinct exact nodeid. The v1 and v2 attempt records and their statuses remain immutable; any further attempt requires another classified source/instrumentation change or a separately defined hypothesis and contract.

corrective_change.change: Apply the cached-reference consistency assertion only when the physical time arrays are exactly identical; retain continuum evaluation and error metrics on every run's own contracted physical grid. No mesh, forcing, model, reference, normalization, acceptance indicator, or budget changed.
corrective_change.demonstrated_cause: The v2 runner compared continuum samples for dt=100 microseconds (80 observations) elementwise with the cached 25 microsecond reference grid (320 observations), before reaching final metrics serialization. The values were computed on the requested grids; the shape mismatch was in a consistency guard, not the mechanical model.
corrective_change.historical_status: The v2 attempt remains PYTEST_FAILED and its durable checkpoints are preserved. The v1 timeout/failure statuses are unchanged.

independent_reference.axial_modulus: lambda+2*mu = E(1-nu)/((1+nu)(1-2nu)) for zero transverse strain; independently calculated from material constants, no QF M or K used.
independent_reference.limitations: This guided-bar benchmark has transverse constraints at every node and is not the free-sided cantilever model of J10. Its reference cannot be transferred to J10 results.
independent_reference.truncation_indicator: compare 512- and 1024-mode displacement histories using the shared continuum peak scale; report, do not qualify.
independent_reference.type: continuum fixed-free axial bar modal series, analytically evaluated convolution for the contracted piecewise-linear force

model.boundary_conditions: UX=0 on x=0; UY=UZ=0 at every mesh node (transverse guidance).
model.excitation: Uniform axial traction-equivalent force on the x=L face; total +1 N, linear ramp 0→1 N over 1 ms, ramp 1→0 N over the next 1 ms, then zero through 8 ms. Same physical pulse for all runs.
model.load_integration: Quadratic TET10 face integration: vertex shape-function integrals are zero for constant face traction and each of the three midside functions receives one third of the triangular face contribution; verify resultant and first moments.

observables_and_indicators.criteria: No formal mechanical correlation or mesh-convergence threshold is set in this exploratory study. Required execution checks are finite histories, PASS Newmark solve status, positive element orientation, exact physical probe, correct 1 N resultant/first moments, and durable checkpoint readback.
observables_and_indicators.error_metrics: RMS and peak absolute displacement difference, additionally divided by one shared global peak absolute continuum displacement over the fixed fine physical time grid.
observables_and_indicators.mesh_comparison: Compare the full-order semidiscrete QF modal oracle against the continuum reference on the common 25 microsecond grid; report Newmark-to-continuum separately because it includes temporal error.
observables_and_indicators.time_comparison: Compare QF Newmark and same-QF-M/K oracle at identical physical times on each contracted step grid; pulse knots are grid points.

resources.limits_semantics: Runner watchdog, sampled process/RSS/temp/archive and free disk are procedural/soft observations except output byte caps; no OS memory quota is claimed.

scope.explicit_non_claim: The same-QF-M/K modal oracle is used only to isolate Newmark integration error and is not independent verification of QF assembly or element mechanics.
scope.hypothesis: The guided axial TET10 Newmark histories can be compared to the full-order same-QF-M/K oracle and an independent continuum fixed-free bar solution after reference self-consistency is limited to exactly matching physical time grids.
scope.route: QF Newmark full-order transient with consistent mass; a distinct QF-assembled M/K modal propagation is used as a time-integration diagnostic.

status: Exploratory only; no qualification or acceptance claim.

supersedes.reason: The v2 solve reached all contracted mesh/time computations and emitted checkpoints, then the harness compared 80-point and 320-point vectors in a guard intended only for identical physical time grids. V3 changes only the guard and uses a separate one-attempt node and ledger entry.
